at tabe.explanation: "At tabe" means "to lose" a game, a fight or a bet: Vi taber kampen (We lose the match). It can also mean "to drop" something: Jeg tabte min telefon (I dropped my phone). For losing an item you cannot find, use at miste (to lose something): Jeg har mistet min nøgle (I have lost my key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **tabe** glasset på gulvet.
sentence.en: I don't want to drop the glass on the floor.

at tabe sig.explanation: "At tabe sig" means "to lose weight": Han har tabt sig ti kilo (He has lost ten kilos). Without sig, at tabe means "to drop" or "to lose": Jeg tabte min telefon (I dropped my phone).

sentence.da: Han vil **tabe sig** og spiser mere grønt.
sentence.en: He wants to lose weight and eats more vegetables.

at tage.explanation: "At tage" means "to take", and it is used in many everyday phrases: tage bussen (take the bus), tage et billede (take a picture), tage bad (take a shower). It can also mean "to go": Jeg tager til København (I am going to Copenhagen). Tag! means "Take it!" or "Here you go!".

sentence.da: Du kan **tage** en kage fra bordet.
sentence.en: You can take a cake from the table.

at tage af.explanation: "At tage af" means "to take off" clothes: Jeg tager jakken af (I take my jacket off). The little word af (off) goes after the thing you take off.

related.en: to put on, to gain weight

sentence.da: Jeg har det varmt og vil **tage af**.
sentence.en: I feel warm and want to take something off.

at tage af bordet.explanation: "At tage af bordet" means "to clear the table", taking the dishes away after a meal: Jeg tager af bordet efter maden (I clear the table after the meal). It is the opposite of setting the table.

sentence.da: Efter maden skal vi **tage af bordet**.
sentence.en: After the meal we have to clear the table.

at tage af sted.explanation: "At tage af sted" means "to set off", to leave for somewhere: Vi tager af sted klokken otte (We set off at eight). Add the place after: Vi tager af sted til Aarhus (We set off for Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage af sted** om ti minutter.
sentence.en: We have to set off in ten minutes.

at tage bad.explanation: "At tage bad" means "to take a shower" or "to take a bath": Jeg tager bad hver morgen (I take a shower every morning). For a soak in the tub, say at tage et karbad (to take a bath in the tub).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage bad** efter løbeturen.
sentence.en: I want to take a shower after the run.

at tage bussen.explanation: "At tage bussen" means "to take the bus" or "to go by bus". The same verb works for other transport: at tage toget (to take the train), at tage taxaen (to take the taxi).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage bussen** til arbejde.
sentence.en: I want to take the bus to work.

at tage det roligt.explanation: "At tage det roligt" means "to take it easy": Jeg tager det altid roligt om søndagen (I always take it easy on Sundays). As a command, Tag det roligt! can also mean "Calm down!".

sentence.da: I weekenden vil jeg **tage det roligt** hjemme.
sentence.en: On the weekend I want to take it easy at home.

at tage en beslutning.explanation: "At tage en beslutning" means "to make a decision". Danes say tage (take) a decision where English says make one: Jeg har taget en beslutning (I have made a decision).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tage en beslutning** inden fredag.
sentence.en: I have to make a decision before Friday.

at tage et billede.explanation: "At tage et billede" means "to take a picture". At tage et foto (to take a photo) means the same. To say what is in the picture, use af (of): tage et billede af maden (to take a picture of the food).

sentence.da: Må jeg **tage et billede** af dig?
sentence.en: May I take a picture of you?

at tage fejl.explanation: "At tage fejl" means "to be wrong", about an opinion or a guess: Du tager fejl (You are wrong). A mistake in a task is en fejl (a mistake): Jeg lavede en fejl (I made a mistake).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt **tage fejl**, men det tror jeg ikke.
sentence.en: I could be wrong, but I do not think so.

at tage fri.explanation: "At tage fri" means "to take time off", which you decide yourself: Jeg tager fri på fredag (I am taking Friday off). When you are allowed to leave, use at få fri (to get off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage fri** på mandag.
sentence.en: I want to take Monday off.

at tage hensyn.explanation: "At tage hensyn" means "to be considerate", or to take others into account: Du skal tage hensyn til de andre (You have to be considerate of the others). Add til (to) before who or what you consider.

sentence.da: Man skal **tage hensyn** til naboerne.
sentence.en: You have to be considerate of the neighbors.

at tage hensyn til.explanation: "At tage hensyn til" means "to take into account", or "to be considerate of": Vi tager hensyn til dem, der sover (We are considerate of those who are sleeping). Du skal tage hensyn til vejret (You have to take the weather into account).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tage hensyn til** naboerne om natten.
sentence.en: We must be considerate of the neighbors at night.

at tage hjem.explanation: "At tage hjem" means "to go home", usually leaving a place such as work or a party. Normally tage means "to take", but in this phrase it means "to go".

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **tage hjem** efter arbejde.
sentence.en: We would like to go home after work.

at tage imod.explanation: "At tage imod" means "to receive / accept": Vi tager imod gæster klokken seks (We receive guests at six). For a gift or help, it means accept: Hun tog imod hjælpen (She accepted the help).

sentence.da: Han vil ikke **tage imod** penge fra os.
sentence.en: He will not accept money from us.

at tage med.explanation: "At tage med" means "to bring along / come along": Jeg tager en jakke med (I bring a jacket along). Må jeg tage med? (May I come along?)

sentence.da: Vil du **tage med** os i biografen?
sentence.en: Do you want to come along with us to the movies?

at tage medicin.explanation: "At tage medicin" means "to take medicine": Jeg tager min medicin hver morgen (I take my medicine every morning). The same verb is used for a pill: at tage en tablet (to take a tablet).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og skal **tage medicin**.
sentence.en: I am sick and have to take medicine.

at tage noter.explanation: "At tage noter" means "to take notes", in class or at a meeting: Jeg tager noter i timen (I take notes in class). Noter is the plural of en note (a note).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage noter**, fordi jeg glemmer alt.
sentence.en: I want to take notes because I forget everything.

at tage op.explanation: "At tage op" means "to pick up", and also "to take up": Jeg tager bogen op fra gulvet (I pick the book up from the floor). Hun tog golf op (She took up golf).

forms.en: I have picked up / taken up

sentence.da: Det vil jeg gerne **tage op** på mødet.
sentence.en: I would like to take that up at the meeting.

at tage på.explanation: "At tage på" means "to gain weight": Jeg har taget på i julen (I gained weight over Christmas). With a trip it means something else: at tage på ferie (to go on vacation).

sentence.da: Hvis du spiser meget kage, kan du **tage på**.
sentence.en: If you eat a lot of cake, you can gain weight.

at tage på ferie.explanation: "At tage på ferie" means "to go on vacation": Vi tager på ferie i juli (We go on vacation in July). To say you are already on vacation, use at være på ferie (to be on vacation).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tage på ferie** til Spanien.
sentence.en: We want to go to Spain on vacation.

at tage sig af.explanation: "At tage sig af" means "to take care of", for people and animals: Hun tager sig af sin syge mor (She takes care of her sick mother). It also works for jobs: Jeg tager mig af opvasken (I will take care of the dishes).

sentence.da: Han vil **tage sig af** hunden i weekenden.
sentence.en: He will take care of the dog on the weekend.

at tage sig tid.explanation: "At tage sig tid" means "to take one's time": Tag dig tid! (Take your time!) Add til at + verb for what you take time for: Han tager sig tid til at tænke (He takes his time to think).

sentence.da: Han vil **tage sig tid** til at tænke.
sentence.en: He wants to take his time to think.

at tage skraldet ud.explanation: "At tage skraldet ud" means "to take out the trash": Min bror tager skraldet ud hver aften (My brother takes out the trash every evening).

forms.en: I have taken out the trash

sentence.da: Kan du **tage skraldet ud**, når du går?
sentence.en: Can you take out the trash when you leave?

at tage tid.explanation: "At tage tid" means "to take time", and Danes usually start with det (it): Det tager tid at lære dansk (It takes time to learn Danish). For something slow, say det tager lang tid (it takes a long time).

sentence.da: Det vil **tage tid** at lære dansk.
sentence.en: It will take time to learn Danish.

at tage toget.explanation: "At tage toget" means "to take the train" or "to go by train". Danish uses at tage (to take) with the type of transport, so you also say at tage taxaen (to take the taxi). The past form tog looks the same as et tog (a train), so the context tells you which is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tage toget** til København.
sentence.en: I want to take the train to Copenhagen.

at tage ud.explanation: "At tage ud" means "to go out": Vi tager ud til stranden (We go out to the beach). It also means "to take out": Jeg tager skraldet ud (I take the trash out).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tage ud** og spise i aften.
sentence.en: We want to go out and eat tonight.

at takke.explanation: "At takke" means "to thank": Jeg vil gerne takke dig (I would like to thank you). It sounds a bit more formal. In daily life, people simply say tak (thanks) or tusind tak (thank you very much).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **takke** dig for hjælpen.
sentence.en: I would like to thank you for the help.

at tale.explanation: "At tale" means "to speak", for a language or a speech: Jeg taler dansk (I speak Danish). For casual chatting, Danes prefer at snakke (to chat, to talk). You say at tale med nogen (to speak with someone) and at tale om noget (to talk about something).

sentence.da: Kan du **tale** dansk?
sentence.en: Can you speak Danish?

at tale med.explanation: "At tale med" means "to talk to" or "to talk with" someone. The little word med (with) comes after it: tale med nogen (to talk to someone). Kan jeg tale med Anna? means "Can I speak to Anna?".

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tale med** dig.
sentence.en: I would like to talk to you.

at tale om.explanation: "At tale om" means "to talk about" a topic: Vi taler om fodbold (We talk about soccer). It is a bit more formal than at snakke om (to chat about), but you can use either in everyday life.

sentence.da: Vi vil **tale om** vejret i dag.
sentence.en: We want to talk about the weather today.

at tale sammen.explanation: "At tale sammen" means "to talk (with each other)", so it needs two or more people: Vi taler sammen hver dag (We talk to each other every day). To name the other person, use at tale med (to talk with): Jeg taler med min mor (I talk with my mother).

sentence.da: Vi skal **tale sammen** om det i morgen.
sentence.en: We need to talk about it tomorrow.

at tale sandt.explanation: "At tale sandt" means "to tell the truth": Han taler altid sandt (He always tells the truth). More often, Danes say at sige sandheden (to tell the truth): Jeg sagde sandheden (I told the truth).

sentence.da: Jeg vil altid **tale sandt**, også når det er svært.
sentence.en: I will always tell the truth, even when it is hard.

at tanke.explanation: "At tanke" means "to refuel", to fill a car with fuel: Jeg tanker bilen (I fill up the car). For an electric car, use at lade (to charge): Jeg lader bilen (I charge the car).

sentence.da: Bilen er næsten tom, og jeg skal **tanke**.
sentence.en: The car is almost empty, and I have to refuel.

at tegne.explanation: "At tegne" means "to draw" with a pencil or pen: Han tegner en hund (He draws a dog). For painting, use at male (to paint): Hun maler et billede (She paints a picture).

sentence.da: Min datter kan **tegne** en hund.
sentence.en: My daughter can draw a dog.

at teste.explanation: "At teste" means "to test", checking whether something works or how good someone is: Vi tester den nye bil (We are testing the new car). For a student, a test is often en prøve (a test or exam).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **teste** os i matematik i morgen.
sentence.en: The teacher will test us in math tomorrow.

at tilbringe.explanation: "At tilbringe" means "to spend (time)": Vi tilbringer weekenden hos mormor (We spend the weekend at Grandma's). It is only for time. For money, say at bruge (to spend): Jeg bruger 100 kroner (I spend 100 kroner).

sentence.da: Vi vil **tilbringe** sommeren i Jylland.
sentence.en: We want to spend the summer in Jutland.

at tilbyde.explanation: "At tilbyde" means "to offer": Jeg tilbyder dig kaffe (I offer you coffee). Han tilbød at hjælpe (He offered to help).

sentence.da: Må jeg **tilbyde** dig en kop te?
sentence.en: May I offer you a cup of tea?

at tilføje.explanation: "At tilføje" means "to add", to put something extra with what is already there: Tilføj mælk (Add milk). It also works for words: Jeg vil tilføje en ting (I want to add one thing). For numbers, say at lægge sammen (to add up).

sentence.da: Du kan **tilføje** lidt salt til suppen.
sentence.en: You can add a little salt to the soup.

at tilgive.explanation: "At tilgive" means "to forgive": Jeg tilgiver dig (I forgive you). You can also name what you forgive: Hun tilgav ham alt (She forgave him everything).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tilgive** dig, fordi du er min ven.
sentence.en: I want to forgive you because you are my friend.

at tillade.explanation: "At tillade" means "to allow": Min mor tillader det ikke (My mother does not allow it). In everyday speech, Danes often use at have lov til (to be allowed to): Jeg har lov til at gå (I am allowed to go).

sentence.da: Min mor vil ikke **tillade** det.
sentence.en: My mother will not allow it.

at tilmelde sig.explanation: "At tilmelde sig" means "to sign up", for a course, a team or an event: Jeg tilmelder mig et dansekursus (I sign up for a dance class). The sig changes with who signs up: Hun tilmelder sig (She signs up), Vi tilmelder os (We sign up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **tilmelde sig** inden fredag.
sentence.en: Everyone has to sign up before Friday.

at tisse.explanation: "At tisse" means "to pee". It is an informal, everyday word used by children, and by adults among friends and family: Jeg skal tisse (I need to pee). In a polite setting, say Jeg skal på toilettet (I need to go to the toilet).

sentence.da: Barnet skal **tisse** på toilettet.
sentence.en: The child has to pee in the toilet.

at tjekke.explanation: "At tjekke" means "to check": Jeg tjekker tiden (I check the time). For a careful check, use at kontrollere (to check carefully); at undersøge (to examine) is for looking into something more deeply.

sentence.da: Jeg skal lige **tjekke** min telefon.
sentence.en: I just need to check my phone.

at tjene.explanation: "At tjene" means "to earn" money: Jeg tjener 300 kroner i timen (I earn 300 kroner an hour). It also means "to serve": Det tjener et formål (It serves a purpose).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tjene** flere penge.
sentence.en: I would like to earn more money.

at tjene penge.explanation: "At tjene penge" means "to earn money" by working: Hun tjener mange penge (She earns a lot of money). To spend money, say at bruge penge (to spend money).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tjene penge** i sommerferien.
sentence.en: I want to earn money during the summer vacation.

at tro.explanation: "At tro" means "to believe" or "to think something is probably true": Jeg tror, det er rigtigt (I think it is right). It is also used for faith: at tro på Gud (to believe in God). For your own taste, use at synes (to think): Jeg synes, det er godt (I think it is good).

related.en: to think / to be of the opinion

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **tro** det!
sentence.en: I can't believe it!

at tro på.explanation: "At tro på" means "to believe in" something or someone: Jeg tror på dig (I believe in you). Without på, at tro means "to think": Jeg tror, det regner (I think it is raining).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tro på** dig.
sentence.en: I would like to believe in you.

at trykke.explanation: "At trykke" means "to press" and also "to print": Jeg trykker på knappen (I press the button). For books and posters, it means printing: Vi trykker bogen (We print the book).

sentence.da: Du skal **trykke** på den grønne knap.
sentence.en: You have to press the green button.

at træde.explanation: "At træde" means "to step", usually with a small word after it: Han trådte ind i huset (He stepped into the house). Hun trådte ud på gaden (She stepped out onto the street).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **træde** på blomsterne.
sentence.en: You must not step on the flowers.

at trække.explanation: "At trække" means "to pull": Jeg trækker i døren (I pull the door). Trække vejret means "to breathe": Han trækker vejret dybt (He breathes deeply).

sentence.da: Vi må **trække** i rebet sammen.
sentence.en: We have to pull on the rope together.

at trække fra.explanation: "At trække fra" means "to subtract": Jeg trækker to fra fem (I subtract two from five). It also means to deduct an amount: Man kan trække det fra i skat (You can deduct it on your taxes).

sentence.da: Du skal **trække fra** og ikke lægge sammen.
sentence.en: You have to subtract and not add.

at trække vejret.explanation: "At trække vejret" means "to breathe". Literally it is to pull the breath, with vejret meaning "the breath". The same word vejret also means "the weather", but the phrase makes the meaning clear.

sentence.da: Du skal **trække vejret** dybt.
sentence.en: You must breathe deeply.

at træne.explanation: "At træne" means "to work out" or "to train": Jeg træner hver dag (I work out every day). It also means "to practice" a skill: træne dansk (to practice Danish).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **træne** tre gange om ugen.
sentence.en: I want to work out three times a week.

at tvinge.explanation: "At tvinge" means "to force". To say what someone is forced to do, add til at (to): Hun tvang ham til at spise (She forced him to eat). Ingen kan tvinge dig (No one can force you).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke **tvinge** mig til at komme.
sentence.en: You cannot force me to come.

at tvivle.explanation: "At tvivle" means "to doubt", usually with på (on): Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer (I doubt that he is coming).

sentence.da: Hun begynder at **tvivle** på sig selv.
sentence.en: She is starting to doubt herself.

at tvivle på.explanation: "At tvivle på" means "to doubt": Jeg tvivler på det (I doubt it). The thing you doubt comes after på: Jeg tvivler på, at han kommer (I doubt that he is coming).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **tvivle på** mig.
sentence.en: Do not doubt me.

at tygge.explanation: "At tygge" means "to chew": Hunden tygger på en pind (The dog chews on a stick). The word tyggegummi (chewing gum) is built from tygge (chew) and gummi (rubber).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **tygge**, fordi min tand gør ondt.
sentence.en: I cannot chew because my tooth hurts.

at tælle.explanation: "At tælle" means "to count": Jeg tæller til ti (I count to ten). Its past forms jeg talte and "jeg har talt" are exactly the same as for at tale (to speak), so the context tells you which is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg kan **tælle** til ti.
sentence.en: I can count to ten.

at tænde.explanation: "At tænde" means "to turn on" a light and also "to light" a candle, a fire or a cigarette: Tænd lyset (Turn on the light). For a TV, a radio or running water, Danes usually say tænde for (turn on) instead. Do not mix it up with at tænke (to think), which looks almost the same.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **tænde** lyset i mørket.
sentence.en: I want to turn on the light in the dark.

at tænde for.explanation: "At tænde for" means "to turn on" something that runs or plays, such as the TV, the radio, the water or the heating. For a light, a candle or a fire, use tænde (to turn on, to light): tænde lyset (turn on the light).

sentence.da: Jeg fryser og vil **tænde for** varmen.
sentence.en: I am cold and want to turn on the heating.

at tænke.explanation: "At tænke" means "to think" in the sense of using your mind: Jeg tænker på dig (I am thinking of you). It goes with på (about). It is not the word for giving an opinion, which is at synes (to think, to have an opinion). Lad mig tænke means "Let me think".

sentence.da: Lad mig **tænke** lidt.
sentence.en: Let me think a little.

at tænke over.explanation: "At tænke over" means "to think about", in the sense of thinking something over carefully: Jeg skal tænke over det (I need to think it over). To have someone in your mind, use at tænke på (to think of): Jeg tænker på dig (I am thinking of you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **tænke over** dit tilbud.
sentence.en: I would like to think about your offer.

at tænke på.explanation: "At tænke på" means "to think of", for having someone or something in your mind: Jeg tænker på dig (I am thinking of you). To think something over carefully, use at tænke over (to think about): Jeg tænker over det (I am thinking it over).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke holde op med at **tænke på** ferien.
sentence.en: I cannot stop thinking about the vacation.

at tænke sig om.explanation: "At tænke sig om" means "to think carefully" before you act or answer: Tænk dig om! (Think carefully!). The small word changes with who is thinking: jeg tænker mig om (I think carefully), han tænker sig om (he thinks carefully).

sentence.da: Man bør **tænke sig om**, før man svarer.
sentence.en: You should think carefully before you answer.

at tømme.explanation: "At tømme" means "to empty": Jeg tømmer skraldespanden (I empty the trash can). It takes everything out of something, so a full thing becomes tom (empty).

sentence.da: Kan du **tømme** opvaskemaskinen for mig?
sentence.en: Can you empty the dishwasher for me?

at tørre.explanation: "At tørre" means "to dry", and also "to wipe": Tøjet tørrer på snoren (The clothes dry on the line). Jeg tørrer bordet af (I wipe the table off).

sentence.da: Håndklæderne skal **tørre** i solen.
sentence.en: The towels have to dry in the sun.

at tørre af.explanation: "At tørre af" means "to wipe", for a table or shelf, and also "to dry dishes": Han tørrer bordet af (He wipes the table). To mop up a spill, use at tørre op (to wipe up).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tørre af** efter middagen.
sentence.en: I have to dry the dishes after dinner.

at tørre støv af.explanation: "At tørre støv af" means "to dust", wiping dust off shelves and tables: Jeg tørrer støv af på hylden (I dust the shelf). The word af stays at the end: Han tørrer støv af hver uge (He dusts every week).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **tørre støv af** på hylderne i dag.
sentence.en: I have to dust the shelves today.

en t-shirt.explanation: "En t-shirt" means "a t-shirt". To say you are wearing one, use have ... på (literally have ... on): Jeg har en t-shirt på (I am wearing a t-shirt).

sentence.da: Jeg har en blå **t-shirt** på i dag.
sentence.en: I am wearing a blue t-shirt today.

en tabel.explanation: "En tabel" means "a table" of rows and columns with information, not a piece of furniture: Tallene står i tabellen (The numbers are in the table). For furniture, use et bord (a table).

sentence.da: Tallene står i en **tabel** på side tre.
sentence.en: The numbers are in a table on page three.

en tablet.explanation: "En tablet" means "a tablet", a flat touchscreen computer. It also means a pill: Jeg tager en tablet mod smerter (I take a pill for pain).

sentence.da: Jeg læser nyheder på min **tablet** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I read the news on my tablet every morning.

en tagrende.explanation: "En tagrende" means "a gutter", the channel along the edge of a roof that carries rainwater away: Tagrenden er fuld af blade (The gutter is full of leaves).

sentence.da: Der ligger mange blade i vores **tagrende**.
sentence.en: There are many leaves in our gutter.

en tallerken.explanation: "En tallerken" means "a plate". At the table you can ask for en tallerken til (one more plate). The stress is at the start: TAL-ler-ken.

sentence.da: Der er mad på min **tallerken**.
sentence.en: There is food on my plate.

en tand.explanation: "En tand" means "a tooth". You say at børste tænder (to brush teeth). En tandlæge (a dentist) is literally a tooth doctor.

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i en **tand** i dag.
sentence.en: One of my teeth hurts today.

en tandbørste.explanation: "En tandbørste" means "a toothbrush". It is built from tand (tooth) and børste (brush): Min tandbørste er blå (My toothbrush is blue).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en ny **tandbørste** i morgen.
sentence.en: I am buying a new toothbrush tomorrow.

en tandlæge.explanation: "En tandlæge" means "a dentist", made from tand (tooth) and læge (doctor). You say Jeg skal til tandlægen (I am going to the dentist) and Jeg skal til lægen (I am going to the doctor).

sentence.da: Min **tandlæge** kigger på mine tænder.
sentence.en: My dentist looks at my teeth.

en tandlægetid.explanation: "En tandlægetid" means "a dentist appointment", built from tandlæge (dentist) and tid (time slot): Jeg har en tandlægetid klokken ti (I have a dentist appointment at ten).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **tandlægetid** i morgen.
sentence.en: I have a dentist appointment tomorrow.

en tandplejer.explanation: "En tandplejer" means "a dental hygienist", someone who cleans your teeth and shows you how to care for them: Jeg har tid hos tandplejeren (I have an appointment with the dental hygienist).

sentence.da: Min **tandplejer** renser mine tænder to gange om året.
sentence.en: My dental hygienist cleans my teeth twice a year.

en tank.explanation: "En tank" means "a tank", especially the fuel tank of a car: Tanken er tom (The tank is empty). It is also the word for the army vehicle.

sentence.da: Bilens **tank** er næsten tom.
sentence.en: The car's tank is almost empty.

en tanke.explanation: "En tanke" means "a thought", something you think: Det var en god tanke (That was a good thought). The phrase at gøre sig tanker om noget (to think about something or worry about it) is common.

sentence.da: Jeg har en **tanke** om, hvad vi kan gøre.
sentence.en: I have a thought about what we can do.

en tankstation.explanation: "En tankstation" means "a gas station". It is built from at tanke (to fill up) and station: Vi skal stoppe ved en tankstation (We need to stop at a gas station).

sentence.da: Tanken er tom, og vi leder efter en **tankstation**.
sentence.en: The tank is empty, and we are looking for a gas station.

en tante.explanation: "En tante" means "an aunt", the sister of a parent or the wife of an uncle. More exactly, faster is your father's sister and "moster" your mother's sister, but tante works for both.

sentence.da: Min **tante** er min mors søster.
sentence.en: My aunt is my mother's sister.

en taske.explanation: "En taske" means "a bag" with a handle or strap. A thin plastic shop bag is en pose (a plastic bag) instead. Words can go in front: en håndtaske (a handbag), en skoletaske (a school bag).

sentence.da: Jeg har bøger i min **taske**.
sentence.en: I have books in my bag.

en tavle.explanation: "En tavle" means "a blackboard", the board at the front of a classroom: Læreren skriver på tavlen (The teacher writes on the board). Add a word in front for other boards: en opslagstavle (a bulletin board).

sentence.da: Der hænger en stor **tavle** i klasseværelset.
sentence.en: A big blackboard hangs in the classroom.

en taxa.explanation: "En taxa" means "a taxi". You say med taxa (by taxi) and at bestille en taxa (to book a taxi).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **taxa** til lufthavnen.
sentence.en: We take a taxi to the airport.

en taxachauffør.explanation: "En taxachauffør" means "a taxi driver", built from taxa (taxi) and chauffør (driver). You can tell the driver where to go with Til banegården, tak (To the railway station, please).

sentence.da: Min far er **taxachauffør** og kører mange passagerer.
sentence.en: My father is a taxi driver and drives many passengers.

en teenager.explanation: "En teenager" means "a teenager", someone between 13 and 19: Min datter er teenager (My daughter is a teenager). Teenagerne sover længe i weekenden (The teenagers sleep late on the weekend).

sentence.da: Min søn er **teenager** og sover længe.
sentence.en: My son is a teenager and sleeps late.

en tegnebog.explanation: "En tegnebog" means "a wallet", the kind that holds banknotes and cards. It is a bit more formal than en pung (a wallet), though both are used.

sentence.da: Jeg har penge og kort i min **tegnebog**.
sentence.en: I have money and cards in my wallet.

en tegnefilm.explanation: "En tegnefilm" means "a cartoon", an animated film: Børnene ser en tegnefilm (The children are watching a cartoon). Do not mix it up with en tegneserie (a comic you read on paper).

sentence.da: Børnene ser en sjov **tegnefilm** i fjernsynet.
sentence.en: The children watch a funny cartoon on TV.

en tegneserie.explanation: "En tegneserie" means "a comic" or "a comic strip": Børn elsker at læse tegneserier (Children love to read comics). A film version is en tegnefilm (a cartoon).

sentence.da: Min datter læser en sjov **tegneserie**.
sentence.en: My daughter is reading a funny comic.

en tegning.explanation: "En tegning" means "a drawing", a picture made with a pencil or pen: Barnet laver en tegning af en hund (The child makes a drawing of a dog). The verb is at tegne (to draw).

sentence.da: Barnet laver en **tegning** af en stor hund.
sentence.en: The child makes a drawing of a big dog.

en tekande.explanation: "En tekande" means "a teapot", the pot you make and pour tea from: Hun hælder te fra tekanden (She pours tea from the teapot).

sentence.da: Vi har en stor **tekande** til gæster.
sentence.en: We have a big teapot for guests.

en teknologi.explanation: "En teknologi" means "a technology", a tool or method built with science: Teknologien udvikler sig hurtigt (The technology is developing fast). Without en, teknologi means technology in general: ny teknologi (new technology).

sentence.da: Ny **teknologi** gør livet nemmere for mange.
sentence.en: New technology makes life easier for many.

en tekst.explanation: "En tekst" means "a text", any piece of written words: Jeg læser en kort tekst (I read a short text). It also means the words of a song (lyrics) and the words under a film: undertekster (subtitles).

sentence.da: Læs den korte **tekst** højt for klassen.
sentence.en: Read the short text out loud for the class.

en telefon.explanation: "En telefon" means "a phone". A mobile phone is en mobiltelefon or, more often, just en mobil. To call someone, say at ringe til: Jeg ringer til dig (I will call you).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig på min **telefon**.
sentence.en: I call you on my phone.

en temperatur.explanation: "En temperatur" means "a temperature", how hot or cold something is. For a high body temperature when you are ill, say at have feber (to have a fever).

sentence.da: Tyve grader er en god **temperatur**.
sentence.en: Twenty degrees is a good temperature.

en teori.explanation: "En teori" means "a theory", an idea that tries to explain something: Det er kun en teori (It is only a theory). It is also the opposite of practice: teori og praksis (theory and practice).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **teori**, men jeg kan ikke bevise den.
sentence.en: I have a theory, but I can't prove it.

en tepose.explanation: "En tepose" means "a tea bag", built from te (tea) and pose (bag): Må jeg få en tepose? (May I have a tea bag?)

sentence.da: Jeg putter en **tepose** i det varme vand.
sentence.en: I put a tea bag in the hot water.

en termokande.explanation: "En termokande" means "a thermos", an insulated jug that keeps drinks hot: Termokanden holder kaffen varm (The thermos keeps the coffee warm). It is built from termo (heat) and kande (jug).

sentence.da: Vi har kaffe i en **termokande** på turen.
sentence.en: We have coffee in a thermos on the trip.

en terning.explanation: "En terning" means "a die" in games, and also "a cube": Slå med terningen (Roll the die). In cooking it means a small cube: en bouillonterning (a bouillon cube).

sentence.da: Du skal slå med en **terning**, og så flytter du brikken.
sentence.en: You roll a die, and then you move the piece.

en terrasse.explanation: "En terrasse" means "a terrace", a paved area next to a house where you sit outside: Vi spiser på terrassen (We eat on the terrace). A cafe can have one too, for outdoor seating.

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at sidde på en **terrasse** om aftenen.
sentence.en: It is lovely to sit on a terrace in the evening.

en terrorist.explanation: "En terrorist" means "a terrorist", a person who uses violence to scare people for a political cause: Politiet anholdt en terrorist (The police arrested a terrorist). The act is terrorisme (terrorism).

sentence.da: Politiet har anholdt en **terrorist** i nat.
sentence.en: The police arrested a terrorist last night.

en teske.explanation: "En teske" means "a teaspoon", both the small spoon and the amount in recipes: Tilsæt to teskeer salt (Add two teaspoons of salt). It is built from te (tea) and ske (spoon).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **teske** sukker i min kaffe.
sentence.en: I take a teaspoon of sugar in my coffee.

en tid.explanation: "En tid" means "a time" or "time" in general: Jeg har tid means "I have time". Danish splits what English calls time: en gang is one occasion (once, twice) and "en time" is an hour. To ask the clock time, say Hvad er klokken? (What time is it?).

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke **tid** i dag.
sentence.en: I do not have time today.

en tid hos lægen.explanation: "En tid hos lægen" means "a doctor's appointment", literally a time at the doctor. En tid alone works for any booked time, such as one at the dentist or hairdresser.

forms.da: Jeg har en tid hos lægen.
Jeg skal have en tid hos lægen.
forms.en: I need to get a doctor's appointment.

sentence.da: Jeg har en **tid hos lægen** i dag.
sentence.en: I have a doctor's appointment today.

en tidsplan.explanation: "En tidsplan" means "a schedule", a plan for when things happen: Jeg følger altid min tidsplan (I always follow my schedule). It is built from tid (time) and plan (plan).

sentence.da: Vi har en stram **tidsplan** i denne uge.
sentence.en: We have a tight schedule this week.

en tidszone.explanation: "En tidszone" means "a time zone": Danmark og Tyskland er i samme tidszone (Denmark and Germany are in the same time zone). New York ligger i en anden tidszone (New York is in a different time zone).

sentence.da: Sverige er i samme **tidszone** som Danmark.
sentence.en: Sweden is in the same time zone as Denmark.

en tiger.explanation: "En tiger" means "a tiger". The g is silent, so it sounds roughly like TEE-uh.

sentence.da: Jeg ser en stor **tiger** i zoo.
sentence.en: I see a big tiger at the zoo.

en tilbudsavis.explanation: "En tilbudsavis" means "a flyer with offers". It is built from tilbud (offer) and avis (newspaper). Stores send it out to show this week's deals: Tilbudsavisen er kommet (The flyer has arrived).

sentence.da: Der er en **tilbudsavis** i postkassen.
sentence.en: There is a flyer with offers in the mailbox.

en tilkørsel.explanation: "En tilkørsel" means "an on-ramp", the road you use to join a highway: Der er kø på tilkørslen (There is a line of cars on the on-ramp). It can also mean any road that leads up to a place.

sentence.da: En **tilkørsel** fører dig op på motorvejen.
sentence.en: An on-ramp leads you up onto the highway.

en tilmelding.explanation: "En tilmelding" means "a registration / sign-up", when you put your name down for a course or an event: Jeg har sendt min tilmelding (I have sent my registration). The matching verb is at tilmelde sig (to sign up).

sentence.da: **Tilmelding** er åben indtil fredag.
sentence.en: Sign-up is open until Friday.

en time.explanation: "En time" means "an hour". It also means a lesson or class, so en dansktime is a Danish lesson. Om en time means "in an hour". For time in general, say tid (time).

sentence.da: Der er tres minutter i en **time**.
sentence.en: There are sixty minutes in an hour.

en ting.explanation: "En ting" means "a thing". The plural looks the same as the singular: mange ting (many things). Example: Hvad er det for en ting? (What is that thing?).

sentence.da: Jeg har mange **ting** i min taske.
sentence.en: I have many things in my bag.

en titel.explanation: "En titel" means "a title", the name of a book, film or song: Hvad er bogens titel? (What is the book's title?). It is also a rank or job name: Hun har titlen professor (She has the title of professor).

sentence.da: Bogen har en spændende **titel**.
sentence.en: The book has an exciting title.

en titelsang.explanation: "En titelsang" means "a theme song", the song that plays at the start of a movie or a show: Titelsangen er fantastisk (The theme song is fantastic). It is built from en titel (a title) and en sang (a song).

sentence.da: Serien har en fed **titelsang**, som jeg altid synger med på.
sentence.en: The series has a cool theme song that I always sing along to.

en tjener.explanation: "En tjener" means "a waiter", for men and women alike. It can also mean "a servant".

sentence.da: En **tjener** bringer maden til bordet.
sentence.en: A waiter brings the food to the table.

en tjeneste.explanation: "En tjeneste" means "a favor" and also "a service": Jeg skylder dig en tjeneste (I owe you a favor). Banken tilbyder en ny tjeneste (The bank offers a new service).

sentence.da: Kan du gøre mig en **tjeneste**?
sentence.en: Can you do me a favor?

en toast.explanation: "En toast" means "a toasted sandwich", usually with ham and cheese: Jeg tager en toast med skinke og ost (I will have a toasted sandwich with ham and cheese). Plain toasted bread is ristet brød (toasted bread).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **toast** med skinke og ost.
sentence.en: I would like a toasted sandwich with ham and cheese.

en togbillet.explanation: "En togbillet" means "a train ticket", built from tog (train) and billet (ticket). Other tickets work the same way: en busbillet (a bus ticket).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **togbillet** til Odense.
sentence.en: I buy a train ticket to Odense.

en togfører.explanation: "En togfører" means "a train conductor", the person in charge of a train and its passengers: Spørg togføreren (Ask the conductor). The conductor is not the one driving, who is called en lokomotivfører (a train driver).

sentence.da: Vores **togfører** siger, at toget er forsinket.
sentence.en: Our conductor says that the train is delayed.

en togrejse.explanation: "En togrejse" means "a train journey", a trip by train: Togrejsen til Berlin tager mange timer (The train journey to Berlin takes many hours).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i toget og nyder en lang **togrejse**.
sentence.en: We sit on the train and enjoy a long train journey.

en togstation.explanation: "En togstation" means "a train station", built from tog (train) and station (station). You say på togstationen (at the train station).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget ved en **togstation**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a train station.

en toiletbørste.explanation: "En toiletbørste" means "a toilet brush", used to clean the toilet. It is built from toilet and børste (brush): Toiletbørsten står ved siden af toilettet (The toilet brush is next to the toilet).

sentence.da: Jeg gør toilettet rent med en **toiletbørste**.
sentence.en: I clean the toilet with a toilet brush.

en toldkontrol.explanation: "En toldkontrol" means "a customs check", where officers look at what you bring into a country: Vi skal igennem toldkontrollen (We have to go through the customs check). It is built from told (customs) and kontrol (check).

sentence.da: Vi skal igennem en **toldkontrol** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: We have to go through a customs check at the airport.

en tomat.explanation: "En tomat" means "a tomato". It joins with other words: tomatsuppe (tomato soup) and tomatsovs (tomato sauce).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en rød **tomat** til salaten.
sentence.en: I cut a red tomato for the salad.

en tommelfinger.explanation: "En tommelfinger" means "a thumb". Tommelfinger op means "thumbs up". Danish says the thumb instead of my thumb: Jeg har ondt i tommelfingeren (My thumb hurts, literally I have pain in the thumb).

sentence.da: Jeg slog min **tommelfinger** med en hammer.
sentence.en: I hit my thumb with a hammer.

en top.explanation: "En top" means "a top", a light shirt with thin straps or no sleeves: Hun har en sort top på (She is wearing a black top). The same word also means the top of something: toppen af bjerget (the top of the mountain).

sentence.da: Det er varmt, og hun tager en **top** på.
sentence.en: It is warm, and she puts on a top.

en tortilla.explanation: "En tortilla" means "a tortilla", a thin round flatbread that is filled and rolled or folded: Hun varmer en tortilla på panden (She heats a tortilla in the pan).

sentence.da: Jeg fylder en **tortilla** med bønner og ost.
sentence.en: I fill a tortilla with beans and cheese.

en torvehal.explanation: "En torvehal" means "a market hall", a covered building with many food stalls, like Torvehallerne in Copenhagen: Torvehallen har frisk fisk og ost (The market hall has fresh fish and cheese).

sentence.da: Vi spiser frokost i en **torvehal** i København.
sentence.en: We eat lunch in a market hall in Copenhagen.

en tradition.explanation: "En tradition" means "a tradition", something a family or country does year after year: Det er en gammel tradition (It is an old tradition). Juletræet er en dansk tradition (The Christmas tree is a Danish tradition).

sentence.da: Det er en gammel **tradition** i vores familie.
sentence.en: It is an old tradition in our family.

en traktor.explanation: "En traktor" means "a tractor", the big farm vehicle with large rear wheels: Bonden kører traktor (The farmer drives a tractor). It pulls heavy loads across the fields.

sentence.da: Landmanden kører **traktor** hen over marken.
sentence.en: The farmer drives a tractor across the field.

en trappe.explanation: "En trappe" means "a staircase" or "stairs": Jeg går op ad trappen (I walk up the stairs). Down is ned ad trappen (down the stairs).

sentence.da: Der er en **trappe** ned til kælderen.
sentence.en: There is a staircase down to the basement.

en tredjedel.explanation: "En tredjedel" means "a third", one of three equal parts. It is built from tredje (third) and del (part): Vi har spist en tredjedel af maden (We have eaten a third of the food).

sentence.da: Jeg har læst en **tredjedel** af bogen.
sentence.en: I have read a third of the book.

en trekant.explanation: "En trekant" means "a triangle", built from tre (three) and kant (edge): Tegn en trekant (Draw a triangle).

sentence.da: Tegn en **trekant** med tre hjørner.
sentence.en: Draw a triangle with three corners.

en tremmeseng.explanation: "En tremmeseng" means "a crib", a baby bed with bars on the sides. It is built from tremmer (bars) and seng (bed): Babyen sover i tremmesengen (The baby sleeps in the crib).

sentence.da: Den lille sover i en **tremmeseng** ved siden af os.
sentence.en: The little one sleeps in a crib next to us.

en troldmand.explanation: "En troldmand" means "a wizard": Troldmanden kan trylle (The wizard can do magic tricks). It is built from trold (troll) and mand (man).

sentence.da: I filmen er han en gammel **troldmand** med skæg.
sentence.en: In the film he is an old wizard with a beard.

en tromme.explanation: "En tromme" means "a drum": Han slår på trommen (He hits the drum). A person who plays it is en trommeslager (a drummer).

sentence.da: Drengen spiller på en stor **tromme**.
sentence.en: The boy plays on a big drum.

en trompet.explanation: "En trompet" means "a trumpet": Jeg har en gammel trompet (I have an old trumpet). To say you play it, leave out en: Han spiller trompet (He plays the trumpet).

sentence.da: Min onkel spiller **trompet** i et orkester.
sentence.en: My uncle plays the trumpet in an orchestra.

en trussel.explanation: "En trussel" means "a threat": Politiet tager truslen alvorligt (The police take the threat seriously). It also works for a danger: en trussel mod miljøet (a threat to the environment).

sentence.da: Han fik en **trussel** på telefonen.
sentence.en: He received a threat on the phone.

en træner.explanation: "En træner" means "a coach", the person who leads a team or a workout: Vores træner er meget sød (Our coach is very kind). It comes from at træne (to train).

sentence.da: Vores **træner** er meget god til at forklare.
sentence.en: Our coach is very good at explaining.

en trøje.explanation: "En trøje" means "a sweater" or "a jumper". Danes also use it for other tops, such as en fodboldtrøje (a soccer shirt).

sentence.da: Jeg har en varm **trøje** på.
sentence.en: I am wearing a warm sweater.

en tulipan.explanation: "En tulipan" means "a tulip", a spring flower that grows from a bulb: Tulipaner kommer frem i april (Tulips come out in April). A bunch of them is en buket tulipaner (a bouquet of tulips).

sentence.da: Jeg har plantet en rød **tulipan** i haven.
sentence.en: I have planted a red tulip in the garden.

en tunge.explanation: "En tunge" means "a tongue", the one in your mouth. At række tunge means "to stick out your tongue".

sentence.da: Lægen sagde: Vis mig din **tunge**.
sentence.en: The doctor said: Show me your tongue.

en tunnel.explanation: "En tunnel" means "a tunnel", a road or train track that goes under the ground, a mountain or the water: Bilen kører ind i tunnelen (The car drives into the tunnel).

sentence.da: Toget kører gennem en lang **tunnel** under havet.
sentence.en: The train goes through a long tunnel under the sea.

en tur.explanation: "En tur" means "a trip" or "a turn". You say at gå en tur (to go for a walk), at tage på tur (to go on a trip) and Det er din tur (It is your turn). A longer, bigger journey is en rejse (a journey).

sentence.da: Vi går en **tur** i parken.
sentence.en: We are going for a walk in the park.

en turist.explanation: "En turist" means "a tourist", someone who visits a place for fun: Der er mange turister i byen (There are many tourists in the city). A person who lives there is en indbygger (a resident).

sentence.da: Som **turist** vil jeg se hele byen.
sentence.en: As a tourist, I want to see the whole city.

en turistattraktion.explanation: "En turistattraktion" means "a tourist attraction", a place many visitors come to see: Tivoli er en kendt turistattraktion (Tivoli is a famous tourist attraction). A shorter word is en seværdighed (a sight).

sentence.da: Den gamle bro er en kendt **turistattraktion**.
sentence.en: The old bridge is a famous tourist attraction.

en tusch.explanation: "En tusch" means "a marker", a pen with thick colored ink: Børnene tegner med tusch (The children draw with markers). A thin pen for writing is en kuglepen (a ballpoint pen).

sentence.da: Børnene tegner med en rød **tusch**.
sentence.en: The children draw with a red marker.

en tv-kanal.explanation: "En tv-kanal" means "a TV channel". Danes often say just kanal (channel): Skift kanal (Change the channel).

sentence.da: Hvilken **tv-kanal** vil du se i aften?
sentence.en: Which TV channel do you want to watch tonight?

en tv-serie.explanation: "En tv-serie" means "a TV series", a show with many episodes. One episode is et afsnit: Vi ser to afsnit i weekenden (We watch two episodes on the weekend).

sentence.da: Jeg ser en ny **tv-serie** om en detektiv.
sentence.en: I am watching a new TV series about a detective.

en tvilling.explanation: "En tvilling" means "a twin": Jeg har en tvilling (I have a twin). It fits both boys and girls: Min tvilling hedder Anna (My twin is called Anna).

sentence.da: Hun er **tvilling**, og hendes søster ligner hende.
sentence.en: She is a twin, and her sister looks like her.

en tvivl.explanation: "En tvivl" means "a doubt". It is mostly used in set phrases: Der er ingen tvivl (There is no doubt) and Jeg har ingen tvivl (I have no doubt).

sentence.da: Jeg er i **tvivl** og kan ikke vælge.
sentence.en: I am in doubt and cannot choose.

en type.explanation: "En type" means "a type" or "a kind": Hvilken type bil har du? (What type of car do you have?) It is also informal for "a guy": en mærkelig type (a strange guy).

sentence.da: Han er en meget flink **type**.
sentence.en: He is a very nice guy.

en tysker.explanation: "En tysker" means "a German", a person from Germany. The word is used for both men and women. You can say either Jeg er tysker or Jeg er tysk (I am German).

sentence.da: Hun er **tysker** og bor i Tyskland.
sentence.en: She is German and lives in Germany.

en tyv.explanation: "En tyv" means "a thief", someone who steals: Tyven tog min taske (The thief took my bag). The action is at stjæle (to steal).

sentence.da: En **tyv** har taget min cykel fra gården.
sentence.en: A thief has taken my bike from the yard.

en tå.explanation: "En tå" means "a toe". The big toe is stortåen (the big toe), and "at gå på tæer" means "to walk on tiptoe".

sentence.da: Jeg slog min **tå** på døren.
sentence.en: I hit my toe on the door.

en tåre.explanation: "En tåre" means "a tear" from the eye: Der løb en tåre ned ad hendes kind (A tear ran down her cheek). Han tørrede en tåre væk (He wiped a tear away).

sentence.da: Hun græd, og der løb en **tåre** ned ad kinden.
sentence.en: She cried and a tear ran down her cheek.

en tændstik.explanation: "En tændstik" means "a match" for lighting a fire or a candle: Har du en tændstik? (Do you have a match?). A match in sports is en kamp (a game), so the two are not the same word.

sentence.da: Jeg tænder bålet med en **tændstik**.
sentence.en: I light the fire with a match.

en tøjbutik.explanation: "En tøjbutik" means "a clothing store". It is made from tøj (clothes) and butik (shop), and Danish often joins words like this: en skobutik (a shoe store).

sentence.da: Jeg køber bukser i en **tøjbutik**.
sentence.en: I buy trousers in a clothing store.

en tøjkurv.explanation: "En tøjkurv" means "a laundry basket". It is tøj (clothes) plus kurv (basket): Det beskidte tøj ligger i tøjkurven (The dirty clothes are in the laundry basket).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger de beskidte sokker i min **tøjkurv**.
sentence.en: I put the dirty socks in my laundry basket.

en tøjstørrelse.explanation: "En tøjstørrelse" means "a clothing size", for example S, M or L. In a shop, ask Har I den i en større størrelse? (Do you have it in a larger size?).

sentence.da: Min **tøjstørrelse** er M, men jeg vil gerne prøve L.
sentence.en: My clothing size is M, but I would like to try L.

en tømrer.explanation: "En tømrer" means "a carpenter", someone who builds with wood, like roofs and house frames: En tømrer bygger tage (A carpenter builds roofs). For furniture, Danes say en snedker (a cabinetmaker).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **tømrer** og arbejder med træ.
sentence.en: My uncle is a carpenter and works with wood.

en tørresnor.explanation: "En tørresnor" means "a clothesline", a cord where you hang clothes to dry: Tøjet hænger på tørresnoren (The clothes are hanging on the clothesline).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger vasketøjet op på en **tørresnor**.
sentence.en: I hang the laundry up on a clothesline.

en tørretumbler.explanation: "En tørretumbler" means "a dryer", a machine that dries clothes with warm air: Tøjet er tørt efter en time i tørretumbleren (The clothes are dry after an hour in the dryer).

sentence.da: Vi har ikke en **tørretumbler**, så tøjet hænger ude.
sentence.en: We do not have a dryer, so the clothes hang outside.

et tag.explanation: "Et tag" means "a roof": Der ligger sne på taget (There is snow on the roof). The same word is also the order Tag! (Take!): Tag en kage! (Take a cake!)

sentence.da: Huset har et rødt **tag**.
sentence.en: The house has a red roof.

et takeaway.explanation: "Et takeaway" means "a takeout meal", food you buy ready-made and eat at home: Jeg henter et takeaway på vej hjem (I pick up a takeout meal on the way home). Many places also deliver: De leverer takeaway (They deliver takeout).

sentence.da: Vi bestiller **takeaway** i aften, fordi vi er trætte.
sentence.en: We are ordering takeout tonight because we are tired.

et tal.explanation: "Et tal" means "a number", like 5 or 12, that you count or calculate with. For a phone number or house number, Danes use et nummer instead.

sentence.da: Fem er et lille **tal**.
sentence.en: Five is a small number.

et talent.explanation: "Et talent" means "a talent", a natural skill: Hun har et talent for sprog (She has a talent for languages). A person with talent is talentfuld (talented).

sentence.da: Hun har et stort **talent** for musik.
sentence.en: She has a great talent for music.

et tandkrus.explanation: "Et tandkrus" means "a toothbrush cup", the small cup in the bathroom that holds your toothbrush: Børsten står i tandkruset (The brush is in the cup).

sentence.da: Jeg putter tandbørsten i et blåt **tandkrus**.
sentence.en: I put the toothbrush in a blue toothbrush cup.

et tastatur.explanation: "Et tastatur" means "a keyboard", the keys you type on. It is built from tast (key): Tryk på en tast (Press a key).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver hurtigt på mit nye **tastatur**.
sentence.en: I type fast on my new keyboard.

et team.explanation: "Et team" means "a team" at work or on a project: Vores team har møde hver mandag (Our team has a meeting every Monday). For a sports team, et hold (a team) is more common.

sentence.da: Mit **team** arbejder sammen om et nyt projekt.
sentence.en: My team is working together on a new project.

et teater.explanation: "Et teater" means "a theater", both the building and the art form: Vi går i teatret i aften (We are going to the theater tonight). A film is shown in a movie theater (en biograf), not et teater.

sentence.da: Vi ser et skuespil i et stort **teater** i aften.
sentence.en: We are watching a play in a big theater tonight.

et tegn.explanation: "Et tegn" means "a sign", something that shows what is happening or what will happen: Det er et godt tegn (That is a good sign). Der er tegn på regn (There are signs of rain).

sentence.da: Hendes smil er et godt **tegn**.
sentence.en: Her smile is a good sign.

et telefonnummer.explanation: "Et telefonnummer" means "a phone number", built from telefon (phone) and nummer (number). Hvad er dit telefonnummer? means "What is your phone number?".

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke dit **telefonnummer**.
sentence.en: I do not have your phone number.

et telt.explanation: "Et telt" means "a tent". To put it up, say at slå et telt op (to pitch a tent): Vi slår teltet op her (We are pitching the tent here).

sentence.da: Vi sover i et **telt** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are sleeping in a tent this weekend.

et termometer.explanation: "Et termometer" means "a thermometer", something that shows how warm or cold it is: Termometeret viser 20 grader (The thermometer shows 20 degrees). It is used for the weather and also for a fever.

sentence.da: Jeg henter et **termometer**, fordi jeg har feber.
sentence.en: I get a thermometer because I have a fever.

et tidspunkt.explanation: "Et tidspunkt" means "a point in time", one exact moment, not a long period: På det tidspunkt var jeg hjemme (At that time I was at home).

sentence.da: Hvilket **tidspunkt** passer dig bedst?
sentence.en: Which time suits you best?

et tilbud.explanation: "Et tilbud" means "an offer" or "a deal". In a shop, på tilbud means "on sale", at a lower price for a short time.

sentence.da: Der er et godt **tilbud** på kaffe.
sentence.en: There is a good deal on coffee.

et tilbudskatalog.explanation: "Et tilbudskatalog" means "a sale catalog", a booklet or web page with offers: Tilbudskataloget kommer med posten (The sale catalog comes in the mail).

sentence.da: Jeg kigger i et **tilbudskatalog** og finder billig mad.
sentence.en: I look in a sale catalog and find cheap food.

et tilfælde.explanation: "Et tilfælde" means "a case" or "a coincidence": I nogle tilfælde er vejen lukket (In some cases the road is closed). Ved et tilfælde (By chance) means nobody planned it. For a case in court, use en sag (a case).

sentence.da: I dette **tilfælde** må vi vente.
sentence.en: In this case we have to wait.

et tip.explanation: "Et tip" means "a tip", a helpful piece of advice: Har du et godt tip? (Do you have a good tip?). For money you leave for service, Danes say drikkepenge (tip money).

sentence.da: Min lærer gav mig et godt **tip** til eksamen.
sentence.en: My teacher gave me a good tip for the exam.

et tog.explanation: "Et tog" means "a train". To say you go by train, Danes say at tage toget, literally to take the train: Jeg tager toget means "I take the train".

sentence.da: Vi tager et **tog** til København.
sentence.en: We take a train to Copenhagen.

et toilet.explanation: "Et toilet" means "a toilet", and also the room that has one. Hvor er toilettet? (Where is the toilet?) is how you ask for the restroom. On the doors, you see Herrer (men) and Damer (women).

sentence.da: Jeg skal på **toilet** og vaske hænder.
sentence.en: I am going to the restroom to wash my hands.

et tordenvejr.explanation: "Et tordenvejr" means "a thunderstorm", weather with thunder and lightning: Der kommer tordenvejr i aften (A thunderstorm is coming tonight). It is built from torden (thunder) and vejr (weather).

sentence.da: Vi bliver inde, fordi der er **tordenvejr**.
sentence.en: We are staying inside because there is a thunderstorm.

et torv.explanation: "Et torv" means "a (market) square", an open space in a town where people meet and sell things: Vi mødes på torvet kl. 12 (We meet on the square at noon).

sentence.da: Der er et lille **torv** midt i byen.
sentence.en: There is a small square in the middle of town.

et trafiklys.explanation: "Et trafiklys" means "a traffic light". It is built from trafik (traffic) and lys (light): Vi stopper ved trafiklyset (We stop at the traffic light).

sentence.da: Bilerne holder stille, når et **trafiklys** er rødt.
sentence.en: The cars stop when a traffic light is red.

et trick.explanation: "Et trick" means "a trick", a clever move that surprises people: Han viser et trick med et kort (He shows a trick with a card). To fool someone, use at narre (to fool).

sentence.da: Hunden lærer et nyt **trick**, og børnene klapper.
sentence.en: The dog learns a new trick, and the kids clap.

et trin.explanation: "Et trin" means "a step" on a stairway or a stage in a process: Der er fem trin op til døren (There are five steps up to the door). For a footstep, use et skridt (a step).

sentence.da: Vi tager det næste **trin** i planen.
sentence.en: We take the next step in the plan.

et træ.explanation: "Et træ" means "a tree", and also "wood" as a material: et bord af træ (a table made of wood). For a large group of trees, Danes say en skov (a forest).

sentence.da: Der er et stort **træ** i haven.
sentence.en: There is a big tree in the garden.

et tv.explanation: "Et tv" means "a TV" and is said te-ve. Watching TV is at se tv (literally to see TV): Vi ser tv i aften (We are watching TV tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i sofaen og ser **tv**.
sentence.en: I sit on the sofa and watch TV.

et tv-program.explanation: "Et tv-program" means "a TV program", one show on TV, for example about nature or food: Hun ser et tv-program om mad (She watches a TV program about food). A show with many episodes is en tv-serie (a TV series).

sentence.da: Der kommer et godt **tv-program** i aften.
sentence.en: A good TV program is coming on tonight.

et tyveri.explanation: "Et tyveri" means "a theft": Der var et tyveri i butikken (There was a theft in the store). The person who does it is en tyv (a thief).

sentence.da: Politiet kommer, fordi der er sket et **tyveri**.
sentence.en: The police are coming because a theft has happened.

et tårn.explanation: "Et tårn" means "a tower", a tall, narrow building or part of a building: Vi kan se tårnet langt væk (We can see the tower from far away).

sentence.da: Der er en flot udsigt fra det høje **tårn**.
sentence.en: There is a nice view from the tall tower.

et tæppe.explanation: "Et tæppe" means both "a rug" and "a blanket": Der ligger et tæppe på gulvet (There is a rug on the floor). Jeg sidder i sofaen med et tæppe (I sit on the sofa with a blanket).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger et **tæppe** over benene.
sentence.en: I put a blanket over my legs.

et tørklæde.explanation: "Et tørklæde" means "a scarf". The second half is klæde (a cloth), which you also see in et håndklæde (a towel).

sentence.da: Jeg har et varmt **tørklæde** på.
sentence.en: I am wearing a warm scarf.

et tørrestativ.explanation: "Et tørrestativ" means "a drying rack" for laundry. It is built from at tørre (to dry) and et stativ (a stand): Vi har et tørrestativ på altanen (We have a drying rack on the balcony).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger tøjet på mit **tørrestativ**.
sentence.en: I hang the clothes on my drying rack.

tag det roligt.explanation: "Tag det roligt" means "take it easy" and "calm down": Tag det roligt, vi har god tid (Take it easy, we have plenty of time). It is also a friendly goodbye: Ses i morgen, tag det roligt (See you tomorrow, take care).

forms.en: You have to take it easy

sentence.da: **Tag det roligt**, vi kommer ikke for sent.
sentence.en: Take it easy, we will not be late.

tak.explanation: "Tak" means "thanks", and Danish also uses it for "please": ja tak means "yes, please" and "Kaffe, tak" means "Coffee, please". You reply to thanks with selv tak (you're welcome).

sentence.da: **Tak** for maden!
sentence.en: Thanks for the food!

tak for det.explanation: "Tak for det" means "thanks for that", a friendly way to thank someone for something that just happened, like advice, help or a small favor. It is more casual than mange tak (thank you very much). You can put other words after tak for: Tak for kaffen means "Thanks for the coffee".

sentence.da: Her er din kaffe. **Tak for det**!
sentence.en: Here is your coffee. Thanks for that!

tak for i dag.explanation: "Tak for i dag" means "thanks for today", said when you part after a day together, such as work, a course or a meeting. Change i dag to i aften (tonight) for an evening, or say tak for sidst (thanks for last time) when you meet again.

forms.da: Tak for i dag, vi ses.

sentence.da: Vi ses i morgen. **Tak for i dag**!
sentence.en: See you tomorrow. Thanks for today!

tak for mad.explanation: "Tak for mad" means "thanks for the meal" (mad is food). You say it at the end of a meal to thank whoever made the food, and the reply is velbekomme (you're welcome, said about food).

forms.da: Tak for mad, det var lækkert.
forms.en: Thanks for the meal, it was delicious.

sentence.da: Maden var lækker. **Tak for mad**!
sentence.en: The food was delicious. Thanks for the meal!

tak for sidst.explanation: "Tak for sidst" means "thanks for last time" and is a friendly hello to someone you met before: Tak for sidst, det var hyggeligt (Thanks for last time, that was nice). Say it when you meet again, not when you leave.

forms.da: Tak for sidst, det var hyggeligt.
forms.en: Thanks for last time, that was nice.

sentence.da: **Tak for sidst**, det var en dejlig aften.
sentence.en: Thanks for last time, it was a lovely evening.

taknemmelig.explanation: "Taknemmelig" means "grateful", and for names what you are grateful for: Hun var taknemmelig for gaven (She was grateful for the gift). It is built from tak (thanks).

sentence.da: Jeg er så **taknemmelig** for din hjælp.
sentence.en: I am so grateful for your help.

tal langsomt.explanation: "Tal langsomt" means "speak slowly". Adding tak (please) makes it polite, and Kan du tale langsommere? (Can you speak more slowly?) is even softer.

forms.da: Jeg forstår, når du taler langsomt
forms.en: I understand when you speak slowly

sentence.da: Jeg er ny her. **Tal langsomt**, tak.
sentence.en: I am new here. Speak slowly, please.

taler du engelsk?.explanation: "Taler du engelsk?" means "Do you speak English?". It is polite to try a little Danish first: Jeg taler lidt dansk (I speak a little Danish). To ask several people, say Taler I engelsk? (Do you all speak English?).

forms.en: I only speak a little Danish.

sentence.da: Undskyld, **taler du engelsk?**
sentence.en: Excuse me, do you speak English?

tandpasta.explanation: "Tandpasta" means "toothpaste": Tandpastaen er i skabet (The toothpaste is in the cabinet). You usually count it in tubes: to tuber tandpasta (two tubes of toothpaste).

sentence.da: Der er ikke mere **tandpasta** i tuben.
sentence.en: There is no more toothpaste in the tube.

tandpine.explanation: "Tandpine" means "toothache". It is built from tand (tooth) and pine (pain). You can also say Jeg har ondt i tanden (literally, I have pain in the tooth).

sentence.da: Jeg har **tandpine** og skal til tandlægen.
sentence.en: I have a toothache and need to go to the dentist.

tape.explanation: "Tape" means "tape" for sticking things together: Kan jeg låne noget tape? (Can I borrow some tape?). You use it for packages, posters and paper.

sentence.da: Jeg har brug for **tape** til pakken.
sentence.en: I need tape for the package.

tapet.explanation: "Tapet" means "wallpaper", the paper you put on a wall instead of paint: Vi sætter tapet op i stuen (We are putting up wallpaper in the living room).

sentence.da: Der er gammelt **tapet** på væggen.
sentence.en: There is old wallpaper on the wall.

te.explanation: "Te" means "tea". It is said like English tay, not like tee. Do not mix it up with ti (ten), which is said like tee.

sentence.da: Jeg drikker varm **te** med citron.
sentence.en: I drink hot tea with lemon.

teknisk.explanation: "Teknisk" means "technical", for machines, methods and how things work: Teknisk set er det muligt (Technically, it is possible).

sentence.da: Der er en **teknisk** fejl i systemet.
sentence.en: There is a technical error in the system.

temmelig.explanation: "Temmelig" means "rather" and "fairly": Der er temmelig mange mennesker (There are rather many people). It is stronger than lidt (a little) but weaker than meget (very).

sentence.da: Vejret er **temmelig** koldt for juni.
sentence.en: The weather is rather cold for June.

tennis.explanation: "Tennis" means "tennis". It goes with at spille (to play): Hun spiller tennis hver torsdag (She plays tennis every Thursday).

sentence.da: Vi spiller **tennis** med en bold.
sentence.en: We play tennis with a ball.

ti.explanation: "Ti" means "ten", said like tee. Do not mix it up with tid (time), which has a d on the end and sounds different.

sentence.da: Efter ni kommer **ti**.
sentence.en: After nine comes ten.

tidlig.explanation: "Tidlig" means "early". To say you do something early, Danish uses tidligt: Jeg står tidligt op (I get up early).

sentence.da: Klokken fem om morgenen er meget **tidlig**.
sentence.en: Five o'clock in the morning is very early.

tidligere.explanation: "Tidligere" means "earlier" and also "former". For time, it means before now: Vi sås tidligere (We met earlier). Before a person or job, it means "former": en tidligere elev (a former student).

sentence.da: Hun har **tidligere** boet i Aarhus.
sentence.en: She has previously lived in Aarhus.

tidligt.explanation: "Tidligt" means "early". Compare Jeg står tidligt op (I get up early) with en tidlig morgen (an early morning): tidligt says when you do something, tidlig goes before a thing like morgen.

sentence.da: Jeg står **tidligt** op klokken fem.
sentence.en: I get up early at five o'clock.

tiende.explanation: "Tiende" means "tenth". It is used for dates: den tiende juni is the tenth of June. In writing, you can use 10. with a dot after the number.

sentence.da: Efter den niende kommer den **tiende**.
sentence.en: After the ninth comes the tenth.

til.explanation: "Til" means "to". Compare Jeg rejser til Danmark (I am traveling to Denmark) with Gaven er til dig (The gift is for you). It also fits meals and holidays: til morgenmad (for breakfast), til jul (at Christmas).

sentence.da: Jeg rejser **til** Aarhus i morgen.
sentence.en: I am traveling to Aarhus tomorrow.

til fælles.explanation: "Til fælles" means "in common" and usually follows at have (to have): Vi har meget til fælles (We have a lot in common). It names what people share, like a hobby or a hometown.

forms.en: What do you have in common?

sentence.da: Vi har mange ting **til fælles**.
sentence.en: We have many things in common.

til højre.explanation: "Til højre" means "to the right", or "on the right". It is used for directions: Drej til højre (Turn right), and for places: Banken er til højre (The bank is on the right).

forms.en: The bank is on the right.

sentence.da: Gå ligeud og drej **til højre**.
sentence.en: Go straight ahead and turn right.

til sidst.explanation: "Til sidst" means "finally" or "in the end", the last step after other things: Vi sang, og til sidst klappede alle (We sang, and finally everyone clapped).

forms.en: In the end we went home

sentence.da: Vi spiste middag, og **til sidst** drak vi kaffe.
sentence.en: We had dinner, and finally we drank coffee.

til tiden.explanation: "Til tiden" means "on time", at the agreed time: Mødet begyndte til tiden (The meeting started on time). It is not early and not late.

sentence.da: Bussen kom **til tiden**, og vi kom ikke for sent.
sentence.en: The bus came on time, and we were not late.

til venstre.explanation: "Til venstre" means "to the left", or "on the left". It is used for directions: Drej til venstre (Turn left), and for places: Posthuset er til venstre (The post office is on the left).

forms.en: The post office is on the left.

sentence.da: Jeg drejer **til venstre** her.
sentence.en: I turn left here.

tilbage.explanation: "Tilbage" means "back" or "left over". Compare Hun går tilbage (She goes back) with Der er to tilbage (There are two left). For the back of your body, use ryg (back) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg kommer snart **tilbage**.
sentence.en: I will be back soon.

tilfreds.explanation: "Tilfreds" means "satisfied" or "content", for being happy with how something turned out: Jeg er tilfreds med resultatet (I am satisfied with the result).

sentence.da: Kunden er **tilfreds** med maden.
sentence.en: The customer is satisfied with the food.

tilfreds med.explanation: "Tilfreds med" means "satisfied with": Jeg er tilfreds med resultatet (I am satisfied with the result). The opposite is utilfreds med (unhappy with): Kunden er utilfreds med servicen (The customer is unhappy with the service).

forms.da: Jeg er tilfreds med min lejlighed.
forms.en: I am satisfied with my apartment.
Are you satisfied with the food?
We are satisfied with the house.

sentence.da: Jeg er **tilfreds med** mit nye job.
sentence.en: I am satisfied with my new job.

tilfældig.explanation: "Tilfældig" means "random" and "by chance": et tilfældigt møde (a chance meeting). To say something happened by accident, use tilfældigvis: Jeg mødte ham tilfældigvis (I happened to meet him).

sentence.da: Jeg valgte en **tilfældig** bog fra hylden.
sentence.en: I chose a random book from the shelf.

tillid.explanation: "Tillid" means "trust", the belief that someone is honest and will not let you down: Tillid tager tid (Trust takes time). You can also say at stole på (to rely on): Jeg stoler på dig (I trust you).

sentence.da: Jeg har stor **tillid** til min læge.
sentence.en: I have great trust in my doctor.

tillykke.explanation: "Tillykke" means "congratulations". Add med (on) and what you are celebrating: tillykke med bilen (congratulations on the car).

sentence.da: **Tillykke** med din nye lejlighed!
sentence.en: Congratulations on your new apartment!

tillykke med fødselsdagen.explanation: "Tillykke med fødselsdagen" means "happy birthday", literally, congratulations with the birthday. It can be shortened to tillykke med dagen (congratulations on the day).

sentence.da: Her er en gave. **Tillykke med fødselsdagen**!
sentence.en: Here is a present. Happy birthday!

tilpas.explanation: "Tilpas" means "just right" or "suitable": Suppen er tilpas varm (The soup is warm enough). With at føle sig (to feel), it means "at ease": Jeg føler mig ikke tilpas (I do not feel at ease).

sentence.da: Vandet er **tilpas** varmt til at bade.
sentence.en: The water is just warm enough for swimming.

tilsammen.explanation: "Tilsammen" means "in total" and also "together": Vi betaler 300 kroner tilsammen (We pay 300 kroner in total). Use sammen (together) when people do something with each other: Vi spiser sammen (We eat together).

forms.en: It is ten kroner in total
There are five of us in total

sentence.da: Vi er ti personer **tilsammen**.
sentence.en: We are ten people in total.

tirsdag.explanation: "Tirsdag" means "Tuesday". Day names are written with a lowercase letter in Danish. På tirsdag means on Tuesday (the coming one), and om tirsdagen or hver tirsdag means every Tuesday.

sentence.da: Efter mandag kommer **tirsdag**.
sentence.en: After Monday comes Tuesday.

tja.explanation: "Tja" means "well" and shows that you are unsure or thinking: Kommer du? Tja, måske (Are you coming? Well, maybe). It is a short sound you say before an answer.

sentence.da: **Tja**, jeg ved ikke helt, hvad jeg skal sige.
sentence.en: Well, I do not quite know what to say.

to.explanation: "To" means "two". It is the same before any word: to biler (two cars) and to huse (two houses). In numbers like 22 the ones come first: toogtyve (twenty-two) is literally two-and-twenty.

sentence.da: En, **to**, tre!
sentence.en: One, two, three!

to gange.explanation: "To gange" means "twice", literally, two times. Use it to say how often: Jeg løber to gange om ugen (I run twice a week).

sentence.da: Én gang, **to gange**, tre gange!
sentence.en: Once, twice, three times!

tofu.explanation: "Tofu" means "tofu", a soft white block made from soybeans that has little taste on its own: Jeg steger tofu med grønsager (I fry tofu with vegetables).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **tofu** i stedet for kød.
sentence.en: I would like tofu instead of meat.

toiletpapir.explanation: "Toiletpapir" means "toilet paper": Jeg skal købe toiletpapir (I need to buy toilet paper). You count it in rolls: en rulle (one roll), to ruller (two rolls).

sentence.da: Vi mangler **toiletpapir**, og jeg går i butikken.
sentence.en: We are out of toilet paper, and I am going to the store.

told.explanation: "Told" means "customs", the place at a border or airport where goods are checked. It also means a tax on goods from abroad: Man skal betale told (You have to pay duty).

sentence.da: Der er lang kø ved **told** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: There is a long line at customs at the airport.

tolv.explanation: "Tolv" means "twelve". Example: Der er tolv måneder i et år (There are twelve months in a year). Compare tolv æg (twelve eggs) with et dusin æg (a dozen eggs).

sentence.da: Efter elleve kommer **tolv**.
sentence.en: After eleven comes twelve.

tom.explanation: "Tom" means "empty", for a bottle, a room, a street or a plate. The opposite is fuld (full), which can also mean "drunk" when it describes a person.

sentence.da: Der er intet vand. Flasken er **tom**.
sentence.en: There is no water. The bottle is empty.

torden.explanation: "Torden" means "thunder", the loud sound in a storm: Jeg hørte torden i nat (I heard thunder last night). Say Det tordner (It is thundering) for what is happening now.

sentence.da: Der var **torden** hele natten.
sentence.en: There was thunder all night.

torsdag.explanation: "Torsdag" means "Thursday". Day names are written with a lowercase letter in Danish. På torsdag means on Thursday (the coming one), and "om torsdagen" means "on Thursdays". Do not mix it up with tirsdag (Tuesday), which looks similar.

sentence.da: Efter onsdag kommer **torsdag**.
sentence.en: After Wednesday comes Thursday.

torsk.explanation: "Torsk" means "cod", both the fish in the sea and the fish on your plate. For the animal, say en torsk (a cod). For the food just say torsk: Vi spiser torsk (We eat cod).

sentence.da: Fiskeren fanger en stor **torsk** i havet.
sentence.en: The fisherman catches a big cod in the sea.

tosset.explanation: "Tosset" means "silly" or "crazy", in a light and friendly way: Du er tosset! (You are silly!). It is much milder than sindssyg (insane).

sentence.da: Hold op, du er så **tosset**!
sentence.en: Stop it, you are so silly!

total.explanation: "Total" means "total", complete with nothing left: en total forandring (a total change). The word totalt (totally) makes another word stronger: Jeg er totalt træt (I am totally tired).

sentence.da: Det var en **total** katastrofe, og alle var kede af det.
sentence.en: It was a total disaster, and everyone was upset about it.

totalt.explanation: "Totalt" means "totally" and makes a word stronger: Jeg er totalt færdig (I am totally finished). You can often use helt (completely) the same way: Jeg er helt færdig (I am completely finished).

sentence.da: Jeg er **totalt** træt efter turen.
sentence.en: I am totally tired after the trip.

traditionel.explanation: "Traditionel" means "traditional", for customs, food and ways of doing things: en traditionel julemiddag (a traditional Christmas dinner). The opposite is moderne (modern).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **traditionel** mad til jul.
sentence.en: We eat traditional food at Christmas.

trafik.explanation: "Trafik" means "traffic" on the roads: Der er meget trafik i dag (There is a lot of traffic today). A traffic jam is en trafikprop.

sentence.da: Der er meget **trafik** på motorvejen i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of traffic on the highway today.

tragisk.explanation: "Tragisk" means "tragic" and is used for very sad events, like accidents and losses: en tragisk ulykke (a tragic accident). It is too strong for a small problem.

sentence.da: Det var en **tragisk** dag, og alle græd.
sentence.en: It was a tragic day, and everyone cried.

travl.explanation: "Travl" means "busy", for a person, a day, a street or a shop. Jeg har det travlt means "I am busy" or "I am in a hurry".

sentence.da: Jeg har meget at lave. Jeg er **travl**.
sentence.en: I have a lot to do. I am busy.

tre.explanation: "Tre" means "three". Example: Jeg har tre børn (I have three children). It stays the same before any word: tre æbler (three apples), tre biler (three cars).

sentence.da: Efter to kommer **tre**.
sentence.en: After two comes three.

tredive.explanation: "Tredive" means "thirty". In 31, the one comes first: enogtredive (thirty-one) is literally one-and-thirty.

sentence.da: Tyve, **tredive**, fyrre.
sentence.en: Twenty, thirty, forty.

tredje.explanation: "Tredje" means "third". It is used for dates too: den tredje oktober is the third of October.

sentence.da: Den første, den anden og den **tredje**.
sentence.en: The first, the second and the third.

tres.explanation: "Tres" means "sixty". Example: Det koster tres kroner (It costs sixty kroner). Do not mix it up with tre (three) or tredive (thirty): tre børn (three children), tres børn (sixty children).

sentence.da: Halvtreds, **tres**, halvfjerds.
sentence.en: Fifty, sixty, seventy.

tretten.explanation: "Tretten" means "thirteen". Example: Min søn er tretten år (My son is thirteen years old).

sentence.da: Tolv, **tretten**, fjorten.
sentence.en: Twelve, thirteen, fourteen.

trist.explanation: "Trist" means "sad". It can describe a person who feels sad (Jeg er trist, I am sad) and also things that are sad or dull, such as a film or gray weather. To say you feel upset, ked af det is also common.
